why: No error signal anywhere: 0 5xx and 0.00% err% on both arms (stable 7343 reqs, canary 2476 reqs) and on every route (/browse, /search, /checkout). The only adverse signal is latency, and the over-time breakdown shows it is warmup, not a steady-state regression: canary p95 falls 210 -> 130 -> 95 -> 94 ms across the four 30 s windows while stable p95 stays flat at 93/94/95/94 ms, so the canary reaches parity by 60 s and holds it for the final 60 s. The whole-test aggregates that look bad (canary p95 177 vs 94, p50 62 vs 34, /checkout p95 215 vs 103) are averages dominated by that first 30-60 s of cold start, so they overstate the steady-state cost. Load is also comparably distributed per pod: the single canary pod served 2476 requests vs roughly 2448 per stable pod, so the canary is not flattered by being under-loaded. Judgement: the steady-state evidence supports promotion. Caveats (judgement, not measured): the sample is one pod and ~2476 requests with zero errors, which cannot rule out a rare fault, and the warmup penalty will recur on each newly started pod. Recommend a staged rollout with readiness/startup probes and surge control rather than replacing all three stable pods at once, and watch 5xx and p95 for the first few minutes after each step.
